verdicts.strongest_argument: Both halves of this finding are already in the two files everyone on this event shares. Each guidance step is verbatim in the captured digest - docs/e38698851525c341f5b4c380fcc23299f7b2a703.txt has 'Sees FY26 adjusted EBITDA $56M-$65M' at the 2025-09-09 print, 'raising its full year fiscal 2026 financial guidance for total revenues to a range of $925 million to $950 million and Adjusted EBITDA to $70 million to $75 million' at 2026-02-03, and 'raising its fiscal 2026 guidance for total revenues to a range of $950M to $975M and Adjusted EBITDA to a range of $85 million to $90 million' at 2026-05-05 - and every one of those was a same-day press release and wire recap. The reaction split the finding leans on is not research either: it is baselines/INNV.json history.moves, which both the hunter and any competing method read straight from the sealed anchor (+37.46% on 2026-02-03, +14.39% on 2025-05-06, -2.81% on 2025-09-09, -17.56% on 2025-11-04). So the claim is an inference over shared public data rather than a fact the corpus failed to publish, and 'this company sandbags its opening guide' after three consecutive raises is structural and known to anyone holding it - age is not novelty. It also cuts both ways: a holder base that has watched three raises discounts a conservative opening guide, which is why the same pattern can produce -2.81% rather than a collapse. What keeps this from scoring higher is real: nothing in the capture assembles the sequence, names the FY-end print as the asymmetric one, or supplies an FY27 consensus to test the bar against, and the +164% re-rating off the low genuinely raises the cost of a soft opening guide.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Same-day earnings recap carrying the FY26 raise to $950-975m revenue and $85-90m adjusted EBITDA.
Same-day recap of the first raise to $925-950m and $70-75m with census guidance unchanged.
'Sees FY26 adjusted EBITDA $56M-$65M' - the original initial guide, published on the day it was set.
'$INNV upgraded' - the only sell-side datapoint in the corpus, dated eighteen days before the print, i.e. coverage was actively revising into this event.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The reaction history the finding cites IS the sealed baseline (six events, median absolute move 11.73%, max 37.46%), so it cannot be evidence of something the baseline misses. quote.json (amc, 09-08 close of 10.52 admissible): 11.04 on 08-26 to 10.75 on 09-04 to 10.52 into the print, run_up_5d -2.59% and run_up_20d -3.49% on 120-250k against a 200,090 average - no accumulation, but also no distribution, and 13.13% off the 52-week high after a 163.66% run off the low. A flat, low-volume run-in is the weakest possible support for a directional claim in either sign.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A dated FY27 revenue or EBITDA consensus - absent from this capture entirely - showing the street has extrapolated the raised FY26 exit rate rather than the company's habit of opening low.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the honest 'reachable but not drawn out' case, and I am not going to inflate it - but three things hold it down. First, the public S-3 filing date is not invisible in the bars: 11.60 on 07-30 to 11.36 on 07-31 (the S-3 acceptance date, 351,600 shares) to 11.23 on 08-03 (347,000), the two highest-volume sessions of that fortnight against a 200,090 average, for a -3.2% two-day drift; whoever was watching EDGAR traded it. Second, the mundane readings are the likely ones and the hunter cannot exclude them because no body is stored: an S-3 five years after a 2021 sponsor-backed IPO is most often a resale or shelf renewal for the pre-IPO holders, and a Form 3 requires no 8-K item 5.02 at all when the filer is a new 10% beneficial owner rather than an officer or director - which is an inflow signal, not an outflow one. The finding itself concedes 'I cannot read the S-3's body and it may simply be a three-year shelf renewal.' Third, the mechanism mostly misses this print: a registered secondary prepared for the post-print window resolves after 8 September, so it is an overhang on the following weeks rather than a component of the reaction, and an effective shelf on its own issues nothing. What I concede is that the corpus genuinely never connects any of this - the 90-message digest does not mention an offering, DRS or S-3 once - and a DRS from an already-listed issuer is a filing type no aggregator surfaces, so if a secondary does price off this shelf the size is unknown and could be material against a $200k-a-day tape.

prior_publication.what_it_says: The registration statement and its effectiveness are public record five weeks before the print; only the 2026-07-17 DRS submission was confidential.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: quote.json: 07-31 volume 351,600 and 08-03 volume 347,000 versus avg_volume_20d of 200,090, with the close going 11.60 -> 11.36 -> 11.23; 08-05 (EFFECT) 11.09 on 170,500 and 08-17 (Form 3) 10.67 on 175,700, both unremarkable. So the public filing registered on the tape and the effectiveness and Form 3 did not. Spot 10.52 is 13.13% off the 52-week high after a 163.66% run, which is the condition that makes a registered secondary plausible - and that condition is visible to everyone in the baseline.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: The S-3 body showing a resale of a specific sponsor block with a share count, or a 424B prospectus supplement dated before the print - either would convert an unread filing type into a sized supply event.

interactions: The two findings use different files (digest versus filings index) and do not share a document. They do interact on direction: INNV#1's most likely benign reading, a sponsor resale shelf, is only attractive to file after the 164% re-rating that INNV#0 treats as the source of downside risk, so both are downstream of the same run-up and should not be counted as two independent negatives.
corpus_limits: No S-3, DRS, Form 3 or 8-K bodies are stored, so I could not verify whether the registration is primary or resale, its dollar size, or who the new Form 3 filer is - the single most decisive fact for INNV#1 is unavailable. The capture contains no analyst notes, no preview and no FY27 consensus for INNV (one bare '$INNV upgraded' post), which is a capture artefact and not evidence that none existed; I have therefore not read the absence of an FY27 estimate as support for INNV#0. No option chain. No tripwire-flagged documents excluded.
